properties.description: Isiro (Haut-Uele hub) -> Dungu -> Faradje -> Aba, then ~18km further to the informal border crossing point. Documented road (MONUSCO-rehabilitated Dungu-Faradje segment); crossing itself is informal/unofficial. Line passes through the snapped Aba border crossing and continues into South Sudan for map visibility.
Aru territory (northern Ituri) -> Lasu (DRC-facing border crossing) -> Yei -> Juba. Historical refugee/trade corridor.

Bunia (Ituri provincial capital, outbreak epicenter) -> Mahagi territory on Lake Albert's western shore, via national road RN27. Documented as the route for fuel and essential goods reaching Bunia from both Uganda and South Sudan.
Wamba (Haut-Uele health zone) -> informal/unofficial crossing points -> Lasu -> Yei County. A more direct path than the Isiro-Dungu-Faradje-Aba route, bypassing those hub towns.
properties.evidence_tier: Field-sourced only - no independent desk corroboration of this exact path

properties.description: Aru (DRC) -> Vurra crossing -> Arua area, Uganda (West Nile sub-region).
properties.evidence_tier: Strong - primary quantified data + independent corroboration

properties.description: Ariwara (DRC) -> Odramacaku crossing -> West Nile sub-region, Uganda. Ariwara is independently documented as a tri-national trade hub (DRC/Uganda/South Sudan).
properties.evidence_tier: Moderate - real, documented crossing, but only subcounty-level coordinates found; one academic source pairs Ariwara with 'Arua' rather than Odramacaku specifically

properties.description: Mahagi (DRC, Lake Albert western shore) -> Goli crossing -> Nebbi area, Uganda.
properties.evidence_tier: Strong - primary quantified data + independent corroboration

properties.description: Beni (Nord-Kivu) -> Kasindi (DRC border town) -> Mpondwe (Uganda, Kasese District) -> onward toward Kasese. Historically the single highest-volume DRC-Uganda crossing in the region; road currently under upgrade. Note: Semliki bridge collapse between Beni and Kasindi has forced a detour via Butembo (Karuruma road, flagged as insecure) - not independently re-verified in the most recent research pass.
properties.evidence_tier: Strong for volume/infrastructure claims; the bridge-collapse detour detail needs re-verification

properties.description: DRC-Uganda border (Arua area) -> transit through Uganda -> Elegu (Uganda, Amuru District, the town directly opposite Nimule) -> Nimule (South Sudan border town) -> Juba, via the formally built Juba-Nimule Road.
properties.evidence_tier: Composite - constructed from verified legs, not one single named source for the whole chain

properties.description: National Road 4 (RN4) - Beni (Nord-Kivu) -> Komanda -> Mambasa -> Nia-Nia (gold-mining village) -> Bafwasende -> Kisangani (Tshopo provincial capital). The single overland route connecting the North Kivu/Ituri epicenter to Tshopo province; matches the appearance of Tshopo-province case zones (Makiso-Kisangani, Mangobo, Wanie-Rukula, Kabondo, Bafwasende) from SitRep 090 onward. Currently unpaved/partially rehabilitated and subject to periodic ADF-related insecurity on the Komanda-Mambasa segment.
properties.evidence_tier: Strong - official road designation + multiple independent corroborating sources

properties.category: Domestic spread corridor (north, Haut-Uele into Bas-Uele)
properties.description: National Road 25 (RN25) - Isiro (Haut-Uele provincial capital) -> Poko -> Dingila -> Bambesa -> Titule -> Buta (Bas-Uele provincial capital), ~500km. Actively under rehabilitation since September 2025 (reported ~60% complete as of May 2026), explicitly intended by the Bas-Uele provincial government to reconnect Bas-Uele and Haut-Uele. Wamba territoire (Haut-Uele, a substantially-affected case zone) is administratively served by the same RN25 network, ~120km south of Isiro, though not itself a through-town on the Isiro-Buta reconstruction project. Timing fits better than a Kisangani-origin route: when Buta recorded its first case (SitRep 090, 12 Aug 2026), Isiro and Wamba already had 37 and 41 cumulative cases respectively, versus only 3 in Makiso-Kisangani at the same date.
properties.evidence_tier: Strong for road existence/routing and active-use signal; inferential for outbreak-specific case-travel link

properties.description: The only one of Mercy Corps' identified Uganda corridors that crosses open water rather than land - a ~3-hour boat crossing on Lake Albert. Bunia -> Kasenyi (in Tchomia health zone) -> Ntoroko, Ntoroko District, Uganda. Geographically the closest of the seven corridors to the outbreak epicenter itself. Ntoroko is the largest fishing town on Lake Albert's southern shore, so movement here is tied to fishing/lake-trade livelihoods rather than road traffic and is structurally difficult to screen with conventional land border-post methods.
properties.evidence_tier: Strong - WHO AFRO explicitly flags this as an Ebola-relevant risk point

properties.description: Crosses the Semliki Valley - the same river system that gives the current outbreak's viral strain (Bundibugyo virus) its name, though that link is historical rather than a present-day transmission factor. No formal customs infrastructure comparable to Vurra or Goli was identified in the source analysis; functions primarily as a community-level crossing route connecting DRC and Ugandan communities on either side of the valley. Geographically distinct from both the Kasindi-Mpondwe corridor to the south and the Kasenyi-Ntoroko lake crossing to the north - its own separate exposure point rather than an alternate path for the same population.
properties.evidence_tier: Moderate - route and confirmed cases well documented; no formal customs infrastructure identified

properties.description: A mature, government-administered crossing (not an informal footpath): Uganda Revenue Authority customs officials are permanently stationed at Busunga, and Uganda has established mandatory health screening, vehicle fumigation, and isolation centres there under Ministry of Health Ebola SOPs. One of only two western border points where Uganda intensified security patrols and health surveillance following the DRC outbreak. IOM tracks Busunga as one of six strategically located flow-monitoring points in Uganda (alongside Mpondwe-Lhubiriha, Butogo, Kanara, Kisoro, and Nsonga), carrying an estimated 380-450 travellers/day. The road continues onward toward Fort Portal and also north along the Rwenzori borderland corridor. Note: exact coordinates for Nobili (Njiapanda) (Irumu Territory, DRC) were not found in available sources - placed here as an estimate directly opposite Busunga/Bundibugyo, near the known Boga health zone; flag for field verification.
properties.evidence_tier: Strong for crossing/infrastructure; waypoints OSM-verified (Nobili place node, Busunga place node)

properties.description: Dungu north on the Dungu-Duru road, crossing at the Nabiapai border post into Yambio County, then east via Yambio, Ibba, Maridi and Mundri to Juba (extension per Mercy Corps team). Context: 3,450 South Sudanese returnees and Congolese nationals were registered at Nabanga, Ibba County, in Sept 2026 after fleeing Ebola fears; South Sudan authorities report screening centres at Gangura, Mediapai and Nabanga. Whether those arrivals used the Nabiapai crossing is not stated in the reporting.
properties.evidence_tier: Mixed - road corridor and arrivals documented; specific crossing used by the Sept 2026 arrivals not confirmed. All waypoints OSM-verified.

properties.description: Yei town to Mundri town; waypoint of travel identified by Mercy Corps team. Indicative straight connector, road alignment not surveyed.
